subject.title: fix: preserve zero sequence ids in sdk events

question: Should the SDK begin emitting distinct canonical normalized IDs for protocol-valid `seq: 0` and `ts: 0`, accepting the resulting value change for existing consumers of `event.id`?
rationale: The implementation fixes a valid-value bug, but normalized IDs are part of the public SDK output and may be used outside the in-package opaque dedupe path.

options.title: Accept canonical zero IDs
options.body: Approve the transition, rebase the branch, and merge with the regression coverage so valid zero components are preserved.

options.title: Preserve legacy output
options.body: Keep the historic ID format only if maintainers determine external consumers require the prior zero-omitting representation, then define a compatible alternative deliberately.

recommendation.title: Accept canonical zero IDs
recommendation.body: Approve the transition, rebase the branch, and merge with the regression coverage so valid zero components are preserved.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the source-level reproduction and proposed implementation, though a current-main SDK history owner should make the final compatibility decision.
